stories.title: Dwight Capital Lends $47M on Houston-Area Apartments Development
stories.excerpt: Hunington Properties has landed $47 million of construction financing to develop a multifamily project in suburban Houston,Commercial Observer has learned. Dwight Capital closed the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)21 (d) 4 construction loan for Hunington’s 279-unit The Vic at Sunterra development in Katy, Texas to be located within the 1,300-acre Sunterra Master Planned Community. The project is slated for completion in fall 2028 by Hunington Residential, the multifamily development arm of Hunington Properties. The non-recourse HUD-backed financing provided the borrower with a 24-month interest-only period followed by a fully amortizing 40-year term to provide a predictable debt service schedule well beyond the construction completion. according to Dwight. David Scheer and Andrew Tichy originated the loan for Dwight. “The property’s location, as well as its standing as the sole multifamily community within the Sunterra master planned community, stand out as key demand drivers, giving residents unique access to amenities including the community’s signature lagoon,” Scheer, managing director at Dwight, said in a statement. “The strength of the local school system adds further appeal, with the property situated within the highly regarded Katy Independent School District and Cross Elementary located right next door.” Located on a 10-acre site at 245 Bartlett Road 35 miles west of Downtown Houston, The Vic at Sunterra project will consist of one and two-bedroom apartments across four three-story buildings. Community amenities in the master-planned community will include a 2.7-acre lagoon with a sand beach, pickleball courts, swimming pool, fitness center and fitness trail. Hunington Properties did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Dwight Capital closed $47M HUD 21(d)4 construction loan for Hunington's 279-unit The Vic at Sunterra in Katy, Texas.
Non-recourse financing includes 24-month interest-only period plus 40-year amortization; completion fall 2028.
Project is sole multifamily within 1,300-acre Sunterra master-planned community, signaling developer confidence in suburban Houston growth.
stories.summary: Hunington Properties secured $47 million in HUD-backed construction financing for The Vic at Sunterra, a 279-unit apartment development in Katy, Texas, with a fall 2028 delivery target. The non-recourse loan features 24 months of interest-only payments followed by a 40-year amortizing term, providing long-term debt certainty. The project's positioning as the sole multifamily component within the 1,300-acre Sunterra master plan underscores developer confidence in suburban Houston market fundamentals.
stories.impact: HUD financing availability and appetite for suburban Houston multifamily signals capital confidence in the metro's job growth and demographic tailwinds, particularly along the I-10 West corridor where Katy sits. The non-recourse structure and extended amortization reduce developer refinance risk, making ground-up construction more feasible in secondary suburban markets.

stories.title: Scale Lending Provides $68M Loan for N.J. Multifamily Building’s Second Phase
stories.excerpt: Capodagli Property Company has secured $67.5 million in construction financing to build the 200-unit second phase of Meridia Rahway Brownstones, a five-story multifamily complex in Rahway, N.J., according to a release. Slate Development’s SCALE Lending provided the debt, which is structured as a 30-month term with two six-month extension options and will retire an existing senior loan while funding final construction of the development. No broker was listed on the transaction, as the deal involved a direct relationship between lender and sponsor. In a statement, John Longo, chief investment officer of Capodagli Property Company, called Slate Property Group “an exceptional lending partner.” Martin Nussbaum, co-founder and principal of Slate Property Group, noted that Capodagli delivered the first phase of the development — a 298-unit building — in 2022 and that “the success of Phase I of Meridia Rahway Brownstones proved out what the market is seeking.” “Capodagli’s deep local roots and strong track record across New Jersey made for exactly the kind of project Scale is built for,” he added. Located at 1999 Elizabeth Avenue in Rahway, a suburb five miles southwest of Elizabeth in New Jersey’s Union County, the site that has become Meridia Rahway Brownstones was initially acquired by Capodagli Property Company in 2012 and has been rezoned from industrial to residential use. The second phase of the development will add 200 units spanning 168,500 square feet, of which six units will be made affordable. The property will also hold 2,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space and 493 parking spaces. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Capodagli Property Company secured $67.5M from Slate/SCALE Lending for 200-unit Phase II of Meridia Rahway Brownstones in Rahway, N.J.
30-month construction term with two 6-month extensions; will retire existing senior debt and fund final construction.
Phase I (298 units) delivered 2022; Phase II success signals strong market validation of the brownstone concept in Rahway.
stories.summary: Capodagli Property Company closed $67.5 million in construction financing from Slate Development's SCALE Lending platform for the 200-unit second phase of Meridia Rahway Brownstones in Rahway, New Jersey. The debt is structured as a 30-month term with two six-month extension options and will refinance an existing senior loan while funding final construction. The successful 2022 delivery of Phase I (298 units) de-risked Phase II underwriting and validated market demand.
stories.impact: Successful Phase II financing and market reception in Rahway signal sustained investor appetite for transit-oriented brownstone multifamily in Northern New Jersey submarkets, particularly where Phase I absorption proved demand and operational performance. Direct lender relationships and developer track records are reducing friction in securing capital for follow-on phases, incentivizing other developers to pursue ground-up multifamily in the NJ Transit corridor.

stories.title: 68-Unit Chicago Lawn Multifamily Portfolio Changes Hands
stories.excerpt: Essex Realty Group completed the sale of the Chicago Lawn Portfolio, a 68-unit, three-building multifamily portfolio located at 6321–31 S. California Avenue, 6355–57 S. California Avenue, and 6400 S. Fairfield Avenue in Chicago’s Chicago Lawn neighborhood. The portfolio sold to Icarus Investment Group for $5.23 million, or $77,000 per unit. Essex Realty Group Directors Jesus Garcia and Joe Kahlhammer represented the seller in the transaction. The Chicago Lawn Portfolio consists of three multifamily buildings situated within close proximity to one another, providing investors with operational efficiency and economies of scale. The portfolio includes a 31-unit building, an 18-unit building, and a 19-unit building. The portfolio offers a diverse unit mix consisting of 12 studio apartments, 31 one-bedroom apartments, 18 two-bedroom apartments, and seven three-bedroom apartments. “The portfolio’s scale and proximity offered an opportunity to acquire 68 units within a compact footprint, allowing for streamlined management across all three properties,” said Garcia. The post 68-Unit Chicago Lawn Multifamily Portfolio Changes Hands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Essex Realty Group sold 68-unit Chicago Lawn Portfolio (three buildings) to Icarus Investment Group for $5.23M ($77K/unit).
Portfolio comprises 31-unit, 18-unit, and 19-unit buildings with diverse mix: studios to 3-bedrooms.
Compact footprint and operational efficiency drove acquisition rationale; reflects value-add/stabilized play in Chicago's South Side.
stories.summary: The Chicago Lawn Portfolio, comprising three multifamily buildings totaling 68 units across three nearby properties in Chicago's Chicago Lawn neighborhood, sold to Icarus Investment Group for $5.23 million, or $77,000 per unit. The portfolio includes a 31-unit, 18-unit, and 19-unit building with a diverse unit mix ranging from studios to three-bedrooms. The buyer emphasized operational efficiency and economies of scale from the compact, consolidated footprint.
stories.impact: Sub-$80K/unit pricing in Chicago South Side signals continued investor appetite for smaller value-add/stabilized portfolios where management consolidation creates arbitrage; limited new supply in older neighborhood pockets keeps acquisition prices compressed, attracting portfolio players and smaller operators seeking operational leverage over ground-up development risk.

stories.title: Lewisville Working with Developers on Town Mall Revamp
stories.excerpt: Hankook Property Management, a partial owner of The Vista, a struggling mall in Lewisville, is working on a redevelopment plan. The company acquired the interior portion, including the theater and former JCPenney, in 2022. The City of Lewisville has been actively facilitating discussions between current property owners and potential developers interested in redeveloping the Vista Mall property. Lewisville officials would have to approve a rezoning once the developers complete their plans. Estimates put the vacancy rate at the mall between 30% and 50%. The plan aims to transform the property into a modern mixed-use destination. The concept calls for more than 1,000 apartments, 34,000 square feet of office, more than 600,000 square feet of retail, a 120-key hotel, 120 townhomes, and open space. In a 2024 Bond Election, voters approved $32 million for the Vista Mall public street infrastructure project. The post Lewisville Working with Developers on Town Mall Revamp appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lewisville, Texas facilitating mixed-use redevelopment of struggling Vista Mall; 30–50% vacancy rate.
Proposed plan: 1,000+ apartments, 120-key hotel, 120 townhomes, 600K+ SF retail, 34K SF office, public open space.
City voters approved $32M bond in 2024 for Vista Street infrastructure; rezoning required for final approval.
stories.summary: The City of Lewisville, Texas is working with developers and Hankook Property Management (partial Vista Mall owner since 2022) on a major mixed-use redevelopment concept that would introduce over 1,000 apartments, 120 townhomes, a 120-key hotel, 600,000+ square feet of retail, and 34,000 square feet of office space. The mall currently carries a 30–50% vacancy rate. Voters approved $32 million in public street infrastructure funding via a 2024 bond election; city rezoning approval will be required for the plan to proceed.
stories.impact: The 1,000+ unit apartment component signals Lewisville's strategic effort to capture suburban Dallas demand via adaptive reuse and mixed-use placemaking; public infrastructure investment ($32M) de-risks the project and improves developer feasibility, likely attracting experienced mixed-use firms. Timing suggests a 2–3 year entitlement window before potential ground-breaking, positioning early movers to capture Lewisville's growth before supply reaches market.

stories.title: 1788 Holdings Acquires 103K-SF Capitol Heights Industrial Property for $15M
stories.excerpt: An investment affiliate of 1788 Holdings, LLC has acquired 51 Ritchie Road, a single-story light industrial building totaling nearly 103,000 square feet of space in the Capitol Heights section of Prince George’s County, Maryland, for $15 million. Situated on nearly eight acres, the site includes two acres of industrial outside storage land and is 100 percent leased and occupied by Bay Crane Mid-Atlantic. CBRE’s Matt Laraway and Luke Wilson represented the seller. 1788 Holdings, a privately-owned real estate investment firm that owns and manages a national commercial real estate portfolio spanning 13 states with a market value exceeding $250 million, was self-represented.Bay Crane Mid-Atlantic was formed after Bay Crane Companies’ 2024 acquisition of United Crane & Rigging and Crane Rental Company, resulting in one of the largest crane companies operating in the Mid-Atlantic region. Delivered in the mid-1950s and renovated in the mid-1970s and in 1997, 51 Ritchie Road is equipped with 18- to 22-foot clear ceiling heights, 11 drive-in doors, and three dock doors, and is surrounded by a considerable amount of paved surface lot. The post 1788 Holdings Acquires 103K-SF Capitol Heights Industrial Property for $15M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 1788 Holdings acquired 103K-SF light industrial building in Capitol Heights, Maryland (Prince George's County) for $15M.
Property 100% leased and occupied by Bay Crane Mid-Atlantic; includes 8 acres with 2 acres outdoor storage.
Asset purchase reflects industrial real estate strength but has no direct multifamily development implication.
stories.summary: An investment affiliate of 1788 Holdings acquired 51 Ritchie Road, a 103,000-square-foot single-story light industrial building in Capitol Heights, Maryland, for $15 million. The property sits on nearly eight acres, including two acres of outdoor storage, and is 100% leased to Bay Crane Mid-Atlantic (formed via Bay Crane's 2024 acquisition of United Crane and Crane Rental Company). CBRE represented the seller; 1788 Holdings self-represented.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance; industrial acquisition in Capitol Heights reflects investor appetite for stabilized, single-tenant industrial assets but does not signal market demand or supply shifts affecting apartment development in the DC/Maryland region.

stories.title: Bank of India, Global Investor IQ-EQ Sign Leases at 1212 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Stawski Partners has two new tenants heading to its Midtown office building at 1212 Avenue of the Americas, Commercial Observer has learned. In the largest deal, Bank of India signed a 20-year, 14,630-square-foot lease for the entire 12th floor of the 24-story office tower in a relocation from 277 Park Avenue, according to landlord broker JLL. Meanwhile, global investment firm IQ-EQ Fund Services agreed to a 10-year, 14,132-square-foot deal on the 14th floor of the property in a move from 250 West 57th Street. JLL did not disclose the asking rent for the building, but the average Midtown office asking rent in the third quarter of 2026 came out to $80.71 per square foot, according to a new report from Colliers. “Stawski Partners has consistently invested in 1212 Avenue of the Americas with an eye toward what tenants want next,” JLL’s Paul Glickman said in a statement. “The initial phase of the [$30 million] renovation modernized the building from the ground up, and this next phase adds the amenities and experience enhancements that leading companies are looking for.” Glickman represented the landlord in both deals alongside Diana Biasotti, Greg Wang and Harrison Potter, while Bank of India was represented by Chris Helgesen, Dirk Hrobsky and Alejandro Alvarez of Cushman & Wakefield as well as Joseph Hilton of Joseph Hilton & Associates. C&W did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Hilton could not be reached for comment. JLL’s Matthew Astrachan, Kristen Morgan, Seth Godnick and Jamie Boast negotiated on behalf of IQ-EQ. The building is also occupied by anti-corruption investigations firm Nardello & Co. which signed a 22,000-square-foot lease in November 2024. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bank of India signed 20-year, 14,630-SF lease on entire 12th floor at 1212 Avenue of the Americas (relocation from 277 Park Ave).
IQ-EQ Fund Services leased 14,132 SF on 14th floor for 10 years (relocation from 250 West 57th Street).
Average Midtown office rent Q3 2026: $80.71/SF; Stawski Partners invested $30M renovation; tenant wins signal leasing momentum.
stories.summary: Stawski Partners secured two large office leases at 1212 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown Manhattan: Bank of India took the entire 12th floor (14,630 square feet, 20-year term) in a relocation from 277 Park Avenue, and IQ-EQ Fund Services leased 14,132 square feet on the 14th floor for 10 years, relocating from 250 West 57th Street. Landlord JLL did not disclose asking rents, but Q3 2026 Midtown average was $80.71 per square foot. Stawski has invested $30 million in renovation and amenities upgrades.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; office leasing strength in Midtown does not displace multifamily demand but underscores continued capital investment in Manhattan's core office submarkets, which competes with multifamily for development capital and may limit land availability in constrained submarkets like Midtown South.

stories.title: Maverick Gaming to Close Eight Casinos in Washington
stories.excerpt: Maverick Washington LLC is set to close eight casinos across Washington, putting 850 people out of work. The affected casinos are Great American Casino in Everett, Chip’s Casino, Macau Casino and Palace Casino in Lakewood, All Star Casino in Silverdale, Casino Caribbean in Yakima, Crazy Moose Casino in Pasco and Coyote Bobs Casino in Kennewick. Kirkland-based Maverick Gaming has operated under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection since last year and has closed five locations since April. Maverick Gaming filed for bankruptcy in July 2025 following a 2024 debt restructuring. The bankruptcy decision caused the closure of the Dragon Tiger Casino, the Palace Casino, the Silver Dollar, and the Roman Casino. The company sent separate letters about each closure to Washington’s Employment Security Department. “Maverick Washington LLC is currently subject to a bankruptcy proceeding and, as part of that proceeding, there could be a potential change of operator and/or owner for the site,” the letters stated. The post Maverick Gaming to Close Eight Casinos in Washington appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Maverick Gaming closing eight Washington casinos (Everett, Lakewood, Silverdale, Yakima, Pasco, Kennewick); 850 job losses.
Company filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy July 2025 after 2024 debt restructuring; has closed nine locations since April 2024.
Potential for site repositioning or change of operator as bankruptcy proceeds; Washington gaming market contraction.
stories.summary: Maverick Washington LLC announced the closure of eight casinos across Washington State, affecting 850 jobs at locations in Everett, Lakewood (three properties), Silverdale, Yakima, Pasco, and Kennewick. The Kirkland-based operator has been operating under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection since July 2025 following a 2024 debt restructuring and has already closed nine locations since April 2024. Bankruptcy filings indicate potential for operator or ownership changes at affected properties.
stories.impact: Significant Washington State job losses and gaming market contraction may temporarily dampen multifamily demand in Everett, Lakewood, and smaller markets (Pasco, Kennewick), though closure of lower-performing properties could free underutilized real estate for repositioning or redevelopment—potential future adaptive-reuse opportunities for multifamily developers if sites are released from bankruptcy.

stories.title: Mohr Capital Sells 1M-SF Industrial Facility Near Indianapolis
stories.excerpt: Mohr Capital announced the sale of Lot 6, a 1,057,350-square-foot industrial facility within Mohr Logistics Park in Whiteland, Indiana. Terms of the transaction and the buyer are not publicly disclosed. Located at 5741 North Graham Road, approximately 20 miles south of Indianapolis, Lot 6 offers modern bulk warehouse space with 40-foot clear heights designed to accommodate large-scale industrial users. The property, currently occupied by Cummins, underscores its ability to support the operational needs of major industrial tenants. Mohr Capital will retain ownership of the remainder of Mohr Logistics Park and continue its long-term investment in the development. Lot 6 is part of Mohr Logistics Park, Mohr Capital’s master-planned industrial development in Whiteland. Covering approximately 475 acres, the park is strategically located along the I-65 corridor and was master planned for nearly 7 million square feet of industrial space. The post Mohr Capital Sells 1M-SF Industrial Facility Near Indianapolis appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Mohr Capital sold 1.06M-SF Lot 6 industrial facility in Mohr Logistics Park (Whiteland, Indiana) to undisclosed buyer.
Property occupied by Cummins; 20 miles south of Indianapolis along I-65 corridor; 40-foot clear heights.
Mohr retains ownership of remaining park; master-planned 475-acre development zoned for ~7M SF industrial capacity.
stories.summary: Mohr Capital announced the sale of Lot 6, a 1,057,350-square-foot industrial facility within Mohr Logistics Park near Whiteland, Indiana, approximately 20 miles south of Indianapolis. The property is currently occupied by Cummins and features 40-foot clear heights suitable for bulk warehouse and large-scale industrial users. Terms and buyer identity were not disclosed. Mohr Capital retains ownership of the remainder of the 475-acre master-planned park, which is master-planned for approximately 7 million square feet of industrial space along the I-65 corridor.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; industrial asset sale does not signal apartment demand shifts in Indianapolis metro, though I-65 South corridor growth and Cummins' continued operations signal broader regional job and population stability that supports underlying multifamily fundamentals in Indianapolis and suburban markets.

stories.title: Law Firm Morgan, Lewis & Bockius Inks 205K SF at 1251 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Global law firm Morgan, Lewis & Bockius has signed a massive lease to relocate its New York City offices. The law firm, which handles corporate mergers and offers specialized consulting, inked a deal for 205,000 square feet at Mitsui Fudosan America’s 1251 Avenue of the Americas, according to a third-quarter Manhattan office report from Colliers. A source close to the deal confirmed the lease. The deal represents a relocation for Morgan, Lewis & Bockius, according to another new office report from Savills. The law firm’s website currently lists its New York City office at 101 Park Avenue near Grand Central Terminal. It is unclear when the law firm will relocate. Spokespeople for the firm did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The asking rent and the length of the lease were also not immediately available, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown Manhattan was $80.71 per square foot during the third quarter, according to Colliers’ most recent data. Newmark is the exclusive leasing agent for 1251 Avenue of the Americas. The brokerage declined CO’s request for comment. It is unclear who brokered the deal for the tenant. Formerly known as the Exxon Building, 1251 Avenue of the Americas is a 54-story office between West 49th and West 50th streets. Other tenants in the building include alternative investment firm LGT Capital Partners, law firm DLA Piper and financial services provider Daiwa Capital Partners. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Morgan, Lewis & Bockius leased 205K SF at 1251 Avenue of the Americas (Mitsui Fudosan America); Manhattan office relocation.
Law firm relocating from 101 Park Avenue near Grand Central Terminal; lease terms and timeline not disclosed.
Q3 2026 Midtown average office rent: $80.71/SF; large law firm consolidation reflects continued Midtown Manhattan office demand.
stories.summary: Global law firm Morgan, Lewis & Bockius signed a 205,000-square-foot lease at Mitsui Fudosan America's 1251 Avenue of the Americas, representing a relocation from its current office at 101 Park Avenue near Grand Central Terminal. Lease terms, duration, and relocation timeline were not disclosed. The average asking rent for Midtown office space in Q3 2026 was $80.71 per square foot, according to Colliers data.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily implication; large office tenant consolidation and relocation in Midtown does not drive apartment demand but signals capital concentration in Manhattan's trophy office buildings, which may constrain development capital availability for multifamily in competing Midtown submarkets.

stories.title: Manhattan’s Available Office Supply Falls to Lowest Level Since 2020: Colliers
stories.excerpt: Despite a slight quarter-over-quarter decline in new deals, Manhattan’s office market saw a robust third quarter of 2026, with leasing volume exceeding both the five-year and 10-year quarterly averages, according to the latest research from Colliers. Manhattan office leasing totaled 10.06 million square feet in July, August and September, driven by large new leases and tenant expansions. The third quarter’s leasing total was 16.2 percent above the five-year quarterly average of 8.66 million square feet and 19.2 percent higher than the 10-year average of 8.44 million square feet. Still, the period’s leasing volume was 8.7 percent less than the 11.02 million square feet leased during the second quarter of 2026. The third quarter marked several milestones in Manhattan’s office leasing, including the first time since 2002 that leasing surpassed 10 million square feet in four consecutive quarters, as well as the strongest third quarter of office activity in Midtown South on record. Midtown South leasing volume reached 4.75 million square feet in the third quarter, driven by large transactions by Anthropic, Havas Health and Snapchat parent company Snap. The third quarter also recorded the lowest available supply of office space in Manhattan since August 2020 at 64.76 million square feet, according to Colliers. Manhattan’s office availability rate was 12.4 percent in the third quarter, representing the 10th consecutive quarter in which availability tightened — the longest stretch since 2007, the firm said. Manhattan’s average office asking rents also rose to the highest levels since July 2020. The average asking rent was $85.08 per square foot in the third quarter, compared to $78.03 per square foot in the second quarter. bullets: Manhattan office leasing Q3 2026: 10.06M SF, up 16.2% vs. 5-year avg (8.66M), up 19.2% vs. 10-year avg (8.44M).
Q3 leasing 8.7% below Q2 2026 (11.02M SF); Midtown South reached 4.75M SF (strongest Q3 on record); first time since 2002 leasing surpassed 10M SF in four consecutive quarters.
Available office supply fell to lowest level since 2020; robust tenant demand and large expansions drive leasing momentum.
stories.summary: Manhattan's office market posted 10.06 million square feet of leasing in Q3 2026, exceeding both the five-year quarterly average (8.66 million square feet) by 16.2% and the ten-year average (8.44 million square feet) by 19.2%, despite an 8.7% decline from Q2's 11.02 million square feet. Midtown South recorded 4.75 million square feet in Q3, marking its strongest third quarter on record and contributing to the first time since 2002 that leasing surpassed 10 million square feet in four consecutive quarters. Manhattan's available office supply has fallen to its lowest level since 2020.
stories.impact: Strong Manhattan office leasing and tightening supply indicate sustained capital and tenant demand concentration in Manhattan's core office markets, which competes aggressively with multifamily for development capital and investor equity. However, four consecutive quarters of 10M+ SF leasing and record Midtown South absorption suggest office market resilience may ease near-term office-to-multifamily conversion pressure, allowing apartment developers to focus on rental-demand growth and new supply in transit-oriented and secondary submarkets rather than adaptive reuse opportunities.
